title: Send Your Name to Saturn's Moon Titan
summary:
You cannot travel to Saturn's moon Titan yet, but your name can. NASA is asking people to send their names to Titan on its Dragonfly mission.

Dragonfly is a flying robot the size of a large car. It runs on nuclear power and NASA plans to launch it in 2028. It should reach Titan in 2034, then fly from place to place across the moon. To send your name, you must sign up before January 15, 2027. The names will be placed on a small chip on the spacecraft.

Titan is a world with an atmosphere, rivers and lakes, seasons, and sweeping dunes. Dragonfly will study the chemistry there to learn about the building blocks of life. It will visit dunes and a young crater called Selk, and it will pick up samples to test inside the craft.

Dragonfly is not the first visitor to Titan. A lander called Huygens touched down there in 2005 and worked for a few hours. But Dragonfly will be the first flying craft to explore Titan up close for years.
why_it_matters: Your name could travel to a faraway moon, and what Dragonfly learns may help us understand how life begins.

Dragonfly is a flying robot that will travel across Titan to study its chemistry and look for the building blocks of life.
An earlier lander called Huygens touched down on Titan and worked for a few hours, but Dragonfly will explore for years.
